title: Probation playbook and handoff brief
notes:
Purpose: quick, actionable playbook for the 1st 8 weeks (probation window) so interviewers + IC mentors can hand off observations into a single, practical eval flow. This is a user-space scratchpad meant to become an internal short-form playbook we can paste into offers/handoffs and share with hiring managers.

High-level intent:
- Make the probation period an evidence-gathering window, not a seat-of-the-pants judgement.
- Create predictable touchpoints and artifacts so decisions are defensible and fast.
- Surface risks early and give focused remediation paths (not vague feedback).

Key assumptions:
- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (example) but keeps flexible for mid/senior infra roles.
- Manager + mentor + peer reviewers available for paired sessions.
- Candidate accepted offer and starts on t0 = first day on calendar.

Suggested timeline (compact):
- Week 0 (pre-start): onboarding checklist sent; first-week calendar blocked (meet manager, buddy, infra overview).
- Week 1: Orientation, infra tour, access, simple first task (local dev + small bug). Manager 1:1 on day 3 to calibrate expectations.
- Week 2: First substantive ticket; pair with mentor. Deliverable: PR with passing tests + short PR description. Manager checkpoint end of week.
- Week 4: Midpoint evaluation. Evidence pulled from PRs, oncall simulation notes, and peer feedback. Quick pass/fix decision: continue, targeted remediation, or pause hiring.
- Week 6: Follow-up on remediation if any. Emphasis on impact and ownership.
- Week 8: Final probation decision and writeup. Decision options: confirmed, extend (with specific goals), or fail (clear reasons + next steps).

Artifacts to collect (discipline-specific):
- PR links with reviewer comments (label: probation/pr).
- Oncall simulation log (timestamped incidents and play/after-action notes).
- Paired design doc or architecture notes (short bullets).
- Synthetic task outcome (if used): e.g., latency regression investigation and mitigation notes.
- Peer sentiment (quick thumbs + 1-line rationale) from 3 people.

Scoring rubric (simple, 4 dimensions) - numeric 1-5, with examples. Keep it short so reviewers actually fill it out.
- Technical craft: writes maintainable code, understands tradeoffs, debugging depth. (1 = avoids code review comments, 5 = instructs team on runtime optimizations)
- Systems judgment: capacity to reason about latency/cost/reliability tradeoffs. (1 = tunnel vision, 5 = good platform-level tradeoffs)
- Collaboration & communication: clarity, responsiveness, triage etiquette. (1 = siloed, 5 = leads/teaches)
- Ownership & impact: takes end-to-end responsibility for delivering and following up. (1 = needs detailed hand-holding, 5 = independently drives work to prod)

Decision thresholds (suggested):
- Confirm hire: average >= 4 and no dimension < 3, and at least 2 strong evidence items (PRs, incident response).
- Extend probation (4 more weeks): average 3-4 or one dimension at 2 with clear remediation plan.
- Fail: average < 3 or any dimension = 1 with no mitigation evidence.

Red flags (quick checklist):
- Repeated missed deadlines without learning or course-correcting.
- Cold rejections of feedback (argumentative + no iteration).
- Inability to debug simple repros in a paired session.
- Major security or compliance blind spots for private deployments.

Green flags (quick checklist):
- Fast, constructive PR iterations + clear commit messages.
- Proactive suggestions to reduce cost/latency even in small tickets.
- Clear ownership of a cross-team handoff (e.g., monitoring dashboard, runbook).
- Positive peer sentiment and willingness to upskill (asks for help).

Sample communication templates (short) - copy/paste friendly:
- Manager 1:1 (week 3): "Quick check-in: how are you finding ramp so far? Any blockers? Two things I noticed: A and B. Can we align on expectations for your next ticket?"
- Midpoint summary to hiring panel: "Evidence: PRs #12,#15; oncall sim notes 2024-10-24; peer thumbs (Alice, Ben, Charlie). Recommendation: Continue with targeted remediation around system testing (mentor: Nina)."

Remediation plan (if used) - must be time-boxed and specific:
- Goal: show repeatable debugging pipeline and improve test coverage for owned subsystem.
- Actions: (1) Pair weekly on incident sim (mentor), (2) Deliver PR to add e2e test by week 6, (3) Shadow oncall rotation for 2 incidents and write postmortem notes.
- Success criteria: passing e2e, positive reviewer feedback on PR, postmortem with clear learning (written).

Handoff checklist for interviewers -> people-ops when offer accepted (short):
- Add hires to probation tracker (spreadsheet link).
- Create label "probation/<name>" for PRs and tickets.
- Schedule mid-probation review invite with hiring panel.
- Assign mentor and share this playbook.

Practical notes for reviewers (how to leave useful feedback):
- Use data: link the specific revision and timestamp. Say: "On PR X line Y, the fix left memory leak because..." vs vague "needs better tests".
- Prefer binary checkpoints in feedback: "Able to reproduce and fix within 90 minutes" or "needs more time".
- Keep comments short and actionable. If you want a longer narrative, paste into the probation review doc rather than PR comments.

Async capture template (one-liner per person, useful for late-night reviewers):
- Name: <reviewer>
- Quick score (1-5): <number>
- Evidence links: <PR/incident>
- 1-line rationale: <why>

Open questions / unresolved bits (for productizing this playbook):
- Should we require an explicit oncall simulation for every infra hire? Pros: reveals debugging. Cons: scheduling overhead and could stress candidate.
- Standard length: 8 weeks vs 12 weeks? Right now 8 seems good but legal/comp constraints to check.
- Where does promo/IC laddering interaction occur if probation is extended? Need HR input.

Quick TODOs (me as author):
- [ ] run this by Nina + Marcus and fold into a shorter Confluence checklist.
- [ ] add standardized spreadsheet template for evidence capture (columns: evidence_url, reviewer, date, score, note).
- [ ] prototype Slack workflow to collect quick thumbs from reviewers into a single doc.

Notes to self (rambling):
- Keep this short. Hiring managers hate form-filling. The friction must be low; we can ask for one PR link + one sim note + three one-line thumbs and still have good signal.
- Emphasize remediation with specific owner and deadline. Too many extended probations float because objectives are fuzzy.
- This playbook should live in Drive as a quick paste-and-go doc, with an associated Confluence page for legal/HR formalities.

Example brief for offer letter append (one sentence):
- "A standard probation window applies for the first 8 weeks during which we will conduct a midpoint and final performance review; outcomes may include confirmation, an extension with a targeted remediation plan, or termination. Details will be provided by the hiring manager."

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally terse — will iterate after the first real case.
